# The Game Awards 2023

American video game award show

| ← [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2022 "The Game Awards 2022") **·**   [The Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards")   **·** [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024 "The Game Awards 2024") → | |

**The Game Awards 2023** was an award show that honored the best [video games of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_games_of_2023 "Video games of 2023"). It was the tenth show hosted by [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley"), creator and producer of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), held with a live audience at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles, California, on December 7, 2023. The preshow ceremony was hosted by Sydnee Goodman. The event was [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across online platforms globally. It featured musical performances from [Loren Allred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loren_Allred "Loren Allred"), [Heilung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heilung "Heilung"), and [Old Gods of Asgard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Gods_of_Asgard "Old Gods of Asgard"), and presentations from celebrity guests, including [Timothée Chalamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothée_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet"), [Christopher Judge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Judge "Christopher Judge"), and [Matthew McConaughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_McConaughey "Matthew McConaughey").

*[Baldur's Gate 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baldur's_Gate_3 "Baldur's Gate 3")* led the show with nine nominations and six wins, including [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year") and Best Performance for [Neil Newbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Newbon "Neil Newbon"). Several new games were announced during the show, including *[Marvel's Blade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel's_Blade "Marvel's Blade")*, *[Lost Records: Bloom & Rage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_Records:_Bloom_&_Rage "Lost Records: Bloom & Rage")*, and *[Visions of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visions_of_Mana "Visions of Mana")*. The show was viewed by over 118 million streams, the most in its history to date,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Views-2) with more than 17,000 co-streams from content creators. Journalists criticized the show for prioritizing announcements and celebrities over awards, and its lack of acknowledgement of [industry layoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023–2024_video_game_industry_layoffs "2023–2024 video game industry layoffs") and the ongoing [Gaza humanitarian crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis "Gaza humanitarian crisis").

## Background

As with previous iterations of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), the 2023 show was hosted and produced by Canadian games journalist [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Engadget_Date-3) He returned as an executive producer alongside Kimmie Kim, and Richard Preuss and LeRoy Bennett returned as director and creative director, respectively.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TGA_Tickets-4) Sydnee Goodman returned as host of the 30-minute preshow, titled Opening Act.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Hours-5) The presentation took place at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles, California, on December 7, 2023,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Engadget_Date-3) and was [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across more than 30 online platforms globally, including [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"), [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), [Steam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_(service) "Steam (service)"), [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok"), [Twitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitch_(service) "Twitch (service)"), [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter"), and [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Polygon_Watch-6)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-7)

Public tickets became available for purchase on November 6,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TGA_Tickets-4) and sold out within a week,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TGA_Tickets_2-8) quicker than any previous year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Interview-9) The show increased security following stage interruptions at [the previous ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2022 "The Game Awards 2022") in December 2022 and [Gamescom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamescom "Gamescom")'s *Opening Night Live* in August 2023.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Security-10) Keighley said the show and preshow aimed for a collective three-hour runtime, like its predecessor.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Hours-5) The Game Awards 2023 was the fourth show to feature Future Class, a list of 50 individuals from across the video game industry who best represent its future, organized by Keighley and Emily Bouchac. The list was announced on December 5, featuring individuals like *[Marvel's Midnight Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel's_Midnight_Suns "Marvel's Midnight Suns")* writer Emma Kidwell, *[The Sims 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sims_4 "The Sims 4")* experience design lead Alister Lee, and accessibility consultant [Ross Minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Minor "Ross Minor").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-GamesHub_Future_Class-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Future_Class-12)

## Winners and nominees

Nominees were announced on November 13, 2023.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Nominees-15) Any game released for public consumption on or before November 17 was eligible for consideration. The nominees were compiled by a jury panel composed of members from over 100 media outlets globally. Specialized juries decided the nominees for categories such as accessibility, adaptation, and [esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports "Esports").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-FAQ-16) Winners were determined between the jury (90 percent) and public voting (10 percent); the latter was held via the official website and [Discord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discord "Discord") server[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-18) until December 6.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Nominees-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Nominees-19) The exception is the Players' Voice award, fully nominated and voted-on by the public, for which voting opened on November 27.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Push_Square_Voice-20) According to Keighley, first-day website voting saw a 73% increase over the previous year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Interview-9)

The Game Awards partnered with Nighttimes and Studio 568 to create an in-game hub world in *[Fortnite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite "Fortnite")*, available from November 14, allowing players to vote for their favorite user-created islands among ten nominees; the winner was announced during the ceremony. Keighley had been seeking to create more in-game events since hosting a live show in *Fortnite* in 2019,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Destructoid_Fortnite-21)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VentureBeat_Fortnite-22) and sought to allow in-game live viewership of the show in the future. He felt it was a more effective advertising technique for the show than traditional marketing like [billboards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard "Billboard").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Interview-9) According to Keighley, the hub world surpassed one million plays within three days, with more than 875,000 unique players.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Keighley_Fortnite-23)

## Reception

### Nominees

Some journalists were surprised by *[Cyberpunk 2077](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_2077 "Cyberpunk 2077")*'s four nominations—twice as many as its original nominations in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2021 "The Game Awards 2021")—particularly due to the game's [troubled launch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_2077#Technical_issues "Cyberpunk 2077").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Cyberpunk-50) Many considered *[Destiny 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny_2 "Destiny 2")*'s Best Community Support nomination poorly timed, coming weeks after layoffs at developer [Bungie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bungie "Bungie"), including much of its community team.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Bungie-51)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VG247_Bungie-52)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-GamesRadar_Bungie-53) Journalists felt several performances were overlooked and suggested Best Performance be split to consider leading and supporting performances to widen its scope.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Snubs-54)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Performance-55)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Performances-56) *TheGamer*'s Stacey Henley found *[Pizza Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizza_Tower "Pizza Tower")*'s nomination for Best Debut Indie Game but not Best Independent Game incongruous.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Indie-57)

The absence of nominations for *[Chained Echoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chained_Echoes "Chained Echoes")* was highlighted as a flaw in the eligibility period for games released the preceding December;[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Snub-58)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-59) some writers opined the show had a [recency bias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recency_bias "Recency bias"), with half the Game of the Year nominees released in October.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Snubs-54)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Starfield-60) Many reporters and players highlighted the sole nomination for *[Starfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starfield_(video_game) "Starfield (video game)")*, a [blockbuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockbuster_(entertainment) "Blockbuster (entertainment)") game from a reputable developer,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-BBC_Nominees-32)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Eurogamer_Starfield-61) though some found it appropriate due to the game's lesser quality compared to its competition.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Starfield-60)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Starfield-62) The lack of nominations for *[Hogwarts Legacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hogwarts_Legacy "Hogwarts Legacy")* was similarly highlighted, with some citing [the game's divisiveness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hogwarts_Legacy#controversy "Hogwarts Legacy") as a possible reason,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Hogwarts-63) though others felt it was due to its relative quality.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-59)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Hogwarts-64)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Escapist_Hogwarts-65) Some lamented the omission of *[Octopath Traveler 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopath_Traveler_2 "Octopath Traveler 2")*,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Mary_Sue_Snub-66)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Snubs-67) and others felt *[Final Fantasy XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_Fantasy_XVI "Final Fantasy XVI")* was snubbed a [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year") nomination.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-59)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Nominees-68)

Several journalists and viewers expressed confusion at *[Dave the Diver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_the_Diver "Dave the Diver")*'s Best Independent Game nomination as its developer, Mintrocket, is a subsidiary of the larger company [Nexon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nexon "Nexon"), which previously claimed the game was "not necessarily" an [indie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_game "Indie game");[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Snubs-54)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Indie-57) *TheGamer*'s Henley wrote that *Baldur's Gate 3* was "technically an entirely independent game" but was likely not considered eligible due to developer Larian Studios's employee count and use of an existing intellectual property.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Indie-57) In response, Keighley said "independent can mean different things to different people" and opted to allow the jury to decide the final selections.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VGC_Indie-69) *TheGamer*'s Jade King called Games for Impact "a locker to stuff all the diverse games into", with four of its six nominees not receiving any other nominations, and felt it was typically limited to independent games despite others fitting the criteria.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Impact-70)

### Ceremony

Before the ceremony, more than 3,000 game industry members, including 79 previous Future Class recipients[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Paste_Gaza-71)—more than half of the 150 members to date[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Eurogamer_Review-72)—signed an open letter calling for a statement to be read during the show addressing the ongoing [Gaza humanitarian crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis "Gaza humanitarian crisis"), supporting the rights of [Palestinians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinians "Palestinians") and calling for a [ceasefire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceasefire "Ceasefire"), and asking the industry to address the dehumanization of people from [South West Asia and North Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Asia_and_North_Africa "South West Asia and North Africa") and their portrayal as villains or terrorists in games. The letter's author, 2021 Future Class recipient Younès Rabii, said it was motivated by [Meg Jayanth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meg_Jayanth "Meg Jayanth")'s withdrawal as a presenter at the [Golden Joystick Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Joystick_Awards "Golden Joystick Awards") in October after being barred from making a statement about Palestinians.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Axios_Gaza-73)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Polygon_Gaza-74)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Gaza-75) *[The Mary Sue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mary_Sue "The Mary Sue")*'s Ana Valens bemoaned the show's lack of response[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Mary_Sue_Gaza-76) and *[Paste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paste_(magazine) "Paste (magazine)")*'s Garrett Martin criticized it as "cowardly".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Paste_Gaza-71) *[Rock Paper Shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Paper_Shotgun "Rock Paper Shotgun")*'s Alice Bell felt the show only would have voiced support if it "was a profitable stance rather than a moral one".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-RPS_Review-77) After the ceremony, developers of nominees *[Goodbye Volcano High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye_Volcano_High "Goodbye Volcano High")* and *[Venba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venba_(video_game) "Venba (video game)")* said they had planned to acknowledge the crisis in their acceptance speeches.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Review-1) Keighley spoke with Future Class members after the show; some members felt he was deflective and unprepared, while others found the meeting productive and hopeful.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Wired_Gaza-78)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Gaza-79) Members gave a presentation to Keighley and Bouchac in December about their negative experiences at the show and lack of resources and opportunities throughout the year; some felt their complaints were taken seriously and that the program consequently improved.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Future_Class-12)

Critics bemoaned the show's lack of acknowledgement of [the video game industry's mass layoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023–2024_video_game_industry_layoffs "2023–2024 video game industry layoffs");[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Review-1)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Verge_Review-99)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-WP_Review-93) *VentureBeat*'s Rachel Kaser found it particularly disappointing considering the show's focus on film and television industry professionals,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VentureBeat_Review_Kaser-100) and *[The Verge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Verge "The Verge")*'s Ash Parrish wrote that "Keighley let video game developers down".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Verge_Review-99) *[Dot Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot_Esports "Dot Esports")*'s Issy van der Velde called it "disappointing but not entirely unexpected" based on the show's history of avoiding acknowledgment.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Dot_Esports_Review-101) *[Game Developer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Developer_(website) "Game Developer (website)")*'s Chris Kerr criticized Keighley's opening speech for calling for unity but failing to address layoffs, and felt the show should spend "less time chasing a hollow sense of legitimacy by curating a showcase that has the cultural awareness and humanity of a shameless [Super Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl "Super Bowl") ad".[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Review-102) The ceremony was picketed by pro-worker protestors advocating for unionization, including members of the Game Workers of Southern California and [SAG-AFTRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAG-AFTRA "SAG-AFTRA");[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Review-81)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Strike-97)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Strike-98) one picket sign read "best year for games, worst year for game workers".[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Review-102)

Some *[Call of Duty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_of_Duty "Call of Duty")* developers criticized presenter [Christopher Judge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Judge "Christopher Judge")'s joke that his 2022 acceptance speech was lengthier than *[Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Modern_Warfare_III "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III")*'s (2023) single-player story campaign.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_CoD-103)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-GamingBolt_CoD-104)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_CoD-105) Current and former developers countered by citing *Call of Duty*'s higher commercial success, though some deleted their responses and said they respected *[God of War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_of_War_(franchise) "God of War (franchise)")*, in which Judge portrays [Kratos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kratos_(God_of_War) "Kratos (God of War)").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Eurogamer_CoD-106)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Push_Square_CoD-107) [Barry Sloane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Sloane "Barry Sloane"), who portrays *Modern Warfare*'s Captain Price, similarly criticized Judge's joke but later wrote "[all's fair in games and war](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/all's%20fair%20in%20love%20and%20war "wikt:all's fair in love and war")" and complimented his performances.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Sloane-108)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Dot_Esports_Sloane-109) [Sledgehammer Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sledgehammer_Games "Sledgehammer Games")'s Darcy Sandall found Judge's joke unexpected "from a peer, at an event that [*[sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")*] supposed to be celebrating this year's achievements in gaming", particularly in light of reports regarding its development involving [crunch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crunch_(video_games) "Crunch (video games)").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_CoD-103)

### Viewership

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/The_Game_Awards_2023_stage_2.png/500px-The_Game_Awards_2023_stage_2.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Game_Awards_2023_stage_2.png)The in-person audience for the Game Awards 2023 at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater")

An estimated 118 million viewers watched the ceremony, the most in the show's history to date[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Views-2) and a 15% increase from the previous year. More than 17,000 content creators co-streamed the event, including over 13,680 on Twitch (a 24% increase) and 4,000 on YouTube. On Twitch, the show peaked at 1.94 million concurrent viewers and saw a 10% increase in total watch time.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-7) The extension "Twitch Predicts The Game Awards" reached almost four million views, with 330,000 concurrent viewers.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Keighley_Twitch-111) On YouTube, the ceremony set a show record with a peak of 1.7 million concurrent viewers, a 35% increase, with over 900,000 on the official channel, a 53% increase.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-7)

| ← [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023 "The Game Awards 2023") **·**   [The Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards")   **·** [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2025 "The Game Awards 2025") → | |

**The Game Awards 2024** was an award show to honor the best [video games of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_games_of_2024 "Video games of 2024"). It was the eleventh show hosted by [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley"), creator and producer of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), and held with a live audience at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles on December 12, 2024, and [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across online platforms globally. It featured musical performances from [d4vd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D4vd "D4vd"), [Royal & the Serpent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_&_the_Serpent "Royal & the Serpent"), [Snoop Dogg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snoop_Dogg "Snoop Dogg"), and [Twenty One Pilots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty_One_Pilots "Twenty One Pilots"), and presentations from celebrity guests including [Harrison Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford "Harrison Ford"), [Hideo Kojima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hideo_Kojima "Hideo Kojima"), and [Aaron Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Paul "Aaron Paul").

*[Astro Bot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro_Bot "Astro Bot")* and *[Final Fantasy VII Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_Fantasy_VII_Rebirth "Final Fantasy VII Rebirth")* led the nominees with seven each, and the former led the show with four wins, including [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year"). The inaugural Game Changer award honored [Amir Satvat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amir_Satvat "Amir Satvat") for helping workers in the industry find jobs amid [mass layoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022–2025_video_game_industry_layoffs "2022–2025 video game industry layoffs"). Several new games were announced, including *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*, *[Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intergalactic:_The_Heretic_Prophet "Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet")*, and *[The Witcher IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Witcher_IV "The Witcher IV")*. The show was viewed by over 154 million streams, the most in its history to date.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Views-1) Journalists praised the game announcements, developer speeches, and deserving winners, though the eligibility of [downloadable content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downloadable_content "Downloadable content") led to mixed responses.

## Background

As with previous iterations of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), the 2024 show was hosted and produced by Canadian games journalist [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley"). He returned as an executive producer alongside Kimmie Kim,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Deadline_Nominees-2) while Richard Preuss returned as director and LeRoy Bennett as creative director and production designer,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Nominees-3)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Preview-4) and Michael E. Peter joined as co-executive producer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-5) The presentation, celebrating the show's tenth anniversary, took place at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles on December 12, 2024,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_Date-6) and was [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across more than 30 online platforms,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Nominees-3) including [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"), [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), [Steam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_(service) "Steam (service)"), [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok"), [Twitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitch_(service) "Twitch (service)"), [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter"), and [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Watch-7) Alternative live streams offering [American Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Sign_Language "American Sign Language") and [audio descriptions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_description "Audio description") were also available on YouTube.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Nominees-3)

The 2024 stage featured more [LED displays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LED_displays "LED displays") than its predecessors, an intentional choice by Bennett to change the show's look each year.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Preview-4) Sydnee Goodman returned as host of the 30-minute preshow, titled Opening Act.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesHub_How-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-FAQ-9) Public tickets became available for purchase on November 1.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_Date-6) Future Class organizer Emily Bouchac indicated that the Future Class initiative—an annual list of 50 individuals from the industry who best represent its future, introduced in 2020—would not induct new members in 2024, instead focusing on valuing existing alumni.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Developer_Future_Class-10)

### Announcements

## Winners and nominees

Nominees were announced on November 18, 2024.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Nominees-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_Nominees-19) Any game released for public consumption on or before November 22 was eligible for consideration,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Eligibility-20) including [downloadable content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downloadable_content "Downloadable content") (DLC), expansions, [remakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_remake "Video game remake"), [remasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_remaster "Video game remaster"), and seasonal content.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_DLC-21) The nominees were compiled by a jury panel composed of members from over 130 media outlets globally;[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Hardcore_Gamer_Nominees-22) ballots were due by November 12.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Eligibility-20) Winners were determined between the jury (90 percent) and public voting (10 percent); the latter was held via the official website and on [Discord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discord "Discord")[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-24) until December 11.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Deadline_Nominees-2)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Nominees-25) The exception was the publicly-voted Players' Voice, for which voting opened on December 2.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Voice-26) Specialized juries decided nominees for categories like accessibility, adaptation, and [esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports "Esports").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Epic_Nominees-27) Two awards—Best Esports Coach and Best Esports Event—were discontinued,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Sheep_Esports-28)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-India_Today-29) while an additional honorary award, Game Changer, was introduced.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-IGN_Game_Changer-30) Approximately 112 million public votes were cast overall, a 25% increase from [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023 "The Game Awards 2023").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Viewers-31)

As with the preceding year, the Game Awards partnered with map developer Studio 568 and artists Nighttimes and Spiral House to create an in-game hub world in *[Fortnite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite "Fortnite")*, allowing players to vote from November 25 to December 11 for their favorite user-created islands among ten nominees selected by Keighley and his team; the winner was announced during the ceremony.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Fortnite-32)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Epic_Fortnite-33) The hub world opened with a [photorealistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photorealistic "Photorealistic") "MetaHuman" model of Keighley,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Aftermath_Fortnite-34) for which he was scanned in to [Unreal Editor for Fortnite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unreal_Editor_for_Fortnite "Unreal Editor for Fortnite") at [3Lateral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3Lateral "3Lateral") in [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Fortnite-35) Several critics found the model strange and [uncanny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncanny "Uncanny").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Aftermath_Fortnite-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_Fortnite-36)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Fortnite-37) Keighley saw the event as "a prototype" for blending the Game Awards and in-game worlds.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GameSpot_Fortnite-38)

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on December 12, 2024.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-IGN_Winners-39) *[Astro Bot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro_Bot "Astro Bot")* became the third game published by [Sony Interactive Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Interactive_Entertainment "Sony Interactive Entertainment") to win [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year") (after *[God of War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_of_War_(2018_video_game) "God of War (2018 video game)")* in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2018 "The Game Awards 2018") and *[The Last of Us Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_of_Us_Part_II "The Last of Us Part II")* in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2020 "The Game Awards 2020")); its nomination marked Sony's ninth consecutive year in the category and thirteenth nomination overall.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_PlayStation-40) It was the second Best Family Game nominee to win the top prize (after *[It Takes Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It_Takes_Two_(video_game) "It Takes Two (video game)")* in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2021 "The Game Awards 2021")).[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_GOTY-41) *[Balatro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balatro "Balatro")* was the first solo-developed Game of the Year nominee (and second card game after *[Hearthstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearthstone "Hearthstone")* in [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2014 "The Game Awards 2014")),[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Balatro-42)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Balatro-43) while *[Black Myth: Wukong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Myth:_Wukong "Black Myth: Wukong")* was the first Chinese-developed nominee[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Nominees-44) and *[Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elden_Ring_Shadow_of_the_Erdtree "Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree")* was the first DLC to be nominated.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-NPR_Nominees-45)

## Reception

### Nominees

Several games saw increased weekly sales following their nominations, including *Final Fantasy VII Rebirth* by 268% and *Metaphor: ReFantazio* by 172%,[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Sales-83) and *Balatro* had its second-highest-earning week on mobile and a 100% increase in [concurrent players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrent_players "Concurrent players") on Steam.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-PocketGamer_Balatro-84)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-PCGamesN_Balatro-85)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Balatro-86) *Balatro*'s nominations pleasantly surprised critics due to its genre,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Snubs-87)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Snubs-89) though some felt other [indie games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_games "Indie games") remained overlooked outside of their dedicated categories.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Snubs-89)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Analysis-90) *[TheGamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TheGamer "TheGamer")*'s Stacey Henley appreciated that Games for Impact "can finally feel like part of the show" as, unlike previous years, some of its nominees were also named in other categories,[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Impact-91) though *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")*'s Keza MacDonald found its nominees incongruous and criteria confusing.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Guardian_Nominees-92) Some felt three of the five Players' Voice nominees being [gacha games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gacha_game "Gacha game") justified the lack of more audience-voted categories.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Dot_Esports_Voice-94)

The omission of Future Class was criticized; *TheGamer*'s Tessa Kaur called it "a loss for the industry",[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Future_Class-95) and *[Digital Trends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Trends "Digital Trends")*'s Giovanni Colantonio considered it a troubling indication that Keighley was attempting to avoid controversy and placate the audience in light of an open letter written by Future Class inductees before the 2023 ceremony.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93) Some critics were puzzled by *[Silent Hill 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_Hill_2_(2024_video_game) "Silent Hill 2 (2024 video game)")*'s Best Narrative nomination as it is a remake of [a 2001 game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_Hill_2 "Silent Hill 2").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Snubs-89)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-AV_Club_DLC-96) *[Dragon Age: The Veilguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon_Age:_The_Veilguard "Dragon Age: The Veilguard")*, *[EA Sports College Football 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EA_Sports_College_Football_25 "EA Sports College Football 25")*, and *[The Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Echoes_of_Wisdom "The Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom")* were considered among the biggest snubs by some critics and viewers.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Snubs-97)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Shacknews_Snubs-98)

Many journalists and viewers criticized *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree*'s Game of the Year nomination as it overshadowed other games,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Snubs-87)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-BBC_GOTY-99)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_DLC-100) though some felt it was justified by its quality and size.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-AV_Club_DLC-96)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Deserves-101) The show's website was updated before nominees were announced to clarify DLC's eligibility, which many predicted was in preparation for *Shadow of the Erdtree*'s divisive nominations;[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_DLC-21)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_DLC-100)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_DLC-102) some viewers erroneously accused Keighley of changing the rules to make it eligible.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Rules-103) Others also felt its eligibility meant DLC was snubbed at previous shows, like *[Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_2077:_Phantom_Liberty "Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty")* and *[Xenoblade Chronicles 3: Future Redeemed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xenoblade_Chronicles_3:_Future_Redeemed "Xenoblade Chronicles 3: Future Redeemed")* in 2023,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Cyberpunk-104)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Destructoid_DLC-105)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Nintendo_Life_DLC-106) and suggested a new category dedicated to DLC would be more appropriate,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-IGN_GOTY-107)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesRadar_DLC-108) though *TheGamer*'s Henley argued there are too few annual releases to justify it.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_DLC-109)

Some journalists considered *Black Myth: Wukong* an [outlier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlier "Outlier") in the Game of the Year nominees and were surprised by its success;[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Snubs-97)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-BBC_GOTY-99) it is the lowest-scoring Game of the Year nominee in the show's history, with 81 out of 100 on [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Metacritic-110)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Metacritic-111) *TheGamer*'s Tessa Kaur felt the game's biggest accomplishment was its popularity, comparing it to *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")*'s [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture") nomination at the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/96th_Academy_Awards "96th Academy Awards").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Wukong-112) Conversely, *[Vice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_(magazine) "Vice (magazine)")*'s Dwayne Jenkins criticized journalists who questioned its deservedness based solely on its critical reception, despite the positive player response; he argued that such discussions are more appropriate for audiences rather than journalists, who should serve as [neutral intermediaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journalistic_objectivity "Journalistic objectivity"), since the awards have no objective criteria.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_Wukong-113)

### Ceremony

*[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")*'s Gene Park called the 2024 ceremony "the best show put on by the Game Awards so far this decade", though he felt the categories required better curation,[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-WP_Review-114) and *[Engadget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engadget "Engadget")*'s Mat Smith wrote that "the Game Awards delivered".[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Engadget_After-115) *[VentureBeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VentureBeat "VentureBeat")*'s [Dean Takahashi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_Takahashi "Dean Takahashi") thought Keighley "redeemed himself" after criticism of the previous ceremony,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Review-49) and *[Push Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push_Square "Push Square")*'s Sammy Barker felt he deserved credit for responding to past criticism, even if some problems remained.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Review-116) *Digital Trends*'s Colantonio called it "the best possible version" of the show, though he criticized the relegation of important awards to the preshow.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93) *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")*'s Issy van der Velde similarly criticized that the esports winners were announced in quick succession during the preshow without acceptance speeches,[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117) and *TheGamer*'s Kaur felt the show remained too long and padded with boring advertisements, though found the reveals surprising "for the first time in a long time".[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Surprises-118)

Journalists deemed the winners deserving, including *Astro Bot*'s Game of the Year award considering its polished and joyful gameplay;[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_GOTY-41)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-WP_Review-114)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Engadget_After-115) the game's sales saw an increase after its win, according to estimates published by Alinea Analytics.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Alinea-119) Many writers considered the game announcements surprising and among the best to date;[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Engadget_After-115)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117) *The Guardian*'s MacDonald compared it to "an old-school [E3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3 "E3") conference".[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Guardian_Review-120) Viewers responded negatively to *[Catly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catly "Catly")*'s reveal ### Viewership

An estimated 154 million viewers watched the ceremony, the most in the show's history to date[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Views-1) and a 31% increase from the previous year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-5) Its figures surpassed the average viewers of the [Super Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII "Super Bowl LVIII") by 30 million, the Academy Awards sevenfold, the [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "66th Annual Grammy Awards") ninefold, and the [World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Series "2024 World Series") tenfold.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Viewers-150) Referencing the viewing figures, [Reggie Fils-Aimé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Fils-Aimé "Reggie Fils-Aimé") called the show "the biggest global entertainment event of our time",[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Viewers-151) though *TheGamer*'s Kaur considered the claim disingenuous, citing the [FIFA World Cup finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_finals "FIFA World Cup finals") and [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"), and the fact that shows like the Super Bowl are generally viewed in groups rather than individually.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Viewers-152)

According to *Streams Charts*, the ceremony peaked at over four million concurrent viewers—the most in its history to date and a 10% increase from 2023—across 1,498 channels, including 1.25 million viewers on the official YouTube broadcast and 397,000 on Twitch.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-5)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Streams-153) More than 15,900 content creators co-streamed the event, including over 11,000 on Twitch and a record 4,500 on YouTube.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Viewers-150) On YouTube, the ceremony peaked at 2.17 million concurrent viewers (a 28% increase), with over 1.3 million on the official channel (a 35% increase).[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesIndustry_Viewers-154) On Twitter, usage of the [hashtag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashtag "Hashtag") #TheGameAwards increased by 150%, with more than 1.59 million posts receiving 6.79 billion [impressions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impression_(online_media) "Impression (online media)").[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Viewers-155)

Com base na pesquisa realizada, aqui está a lista dos modelos de linguagem **decoder-only** (arquitetura GPT-like) voltados para **português**, lançados **até dezembro de 2024**:

---

## Modelos Decoder-Only para Português (lançados até dez/2024)

### 🇧🇷 Português Brasileiro (PT-BR)

---

### Detalhes importantes

#### 🔹 Modelos treinados **do zero** para português (sem base externa):
1. **TeenyTinyLlama** (jan/2024) — dois modelos compactos (~160M e ~460M), pré-treinados exclusivamente em PT-BR com arquitetura Transformer decoder-only baseada em Llama.
2. **Tucano família** (nov/2024) — série de modelos (160M, 630M, 1B, 2.4B) pré-treinados nativamente no corpus **GigaVerbo** (~200 bilhões de tokens de português). Embora usem arquitetura inspirada no Llama, foram treinados do zero com vocabulário próprio de 32k tokens e dados em PT.

#### 🔹 Modelos via **fine-tuning / pré-treinamento contínuo** sobre bases existentes:
- **Gervásio 7B PTBR** (fev/2024) — fine-tuning do LLaMA 2 7B com foco em prompts em português.
- **Gaia 4B** (mai/2024) — pré-treinamento contínuo (CPT) da Gemma-3 4B em PT-BR.
- **Aira 2 PT 1.7B** (out/2024) — fine-tuning do BLOOM.
- **Boto 9B** (jul/2024) — fine-tuning do Gemma 2 9B.
- Diversos **Cabra** (mar–jul/2024) — fine-tuning de Qwen, Mistral, Llama 3.
- **Bode 7B/13B** e **Phi-Bode** — fine-tuning de LLaMA 2 e Phi-2.
- **Carvalho_pt-gl-1.3B** — fine-tuning multilíngue.

#### 🔹 Modelos **privados / sem pesos abertos** (disponíveis apenas via API ou descritos em relatórios):
- **Sabiá-3** (abr/2024) — Maritaca AI, disponível via API e chat, sem pesos públicos.
- **Amazônia IA** (ago/2024) — Widelabs + Oracle/NVIDIA, proprietário.
- **SoberanIA** — Governo do Piauí, ainda não lançado formalmente.

---

**2023 (relevante, anterior ao corte):**

conversa_com_ferramentas.content:
## Tucano: Advancing Neural Text Generation for Portuguese

University of Bonn  
1Center for Science and Thought  
2Helmholtz-Institut für Strahlen- und Kernphysik  
3Institute for Science and Ethics  
4Institute for Computer Science

[Patterns](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patter.2025.101325) [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07854) [Code](https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/Tucano) [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR)

[https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/videos/banner_video.mp4](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/videos/banner_video.mp4)

## Tucano is a series of natively pre-trained open-source Portuguese language models. We release them under the permissive Apache 2.0 license on [GitHub](https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/Tucano) and [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR) for community use and further development.

## Abstract

Significant advances have been made in natural language processing in recent years. However, our current deep learning approach to language
 modeling requires substantial resources in terms of data and computation. One of the side effects of this data-hungry
 paradigm is the current schism between languages, separating those considered high-resource, where most of the development
 happens and resources are available, and the low-resource ones, which struggle to attain the same level of performance and
 autonomy. This study aims to introduce a new set of resources to stimulate the future development of neural text generation
 in Portuguese. In this work, we document the development of ***GigaVerbo***, a concatenation of deduplicated
 Portuguese text corpora amounting to 200 billion tokens. Via this corpus, we trained a series of decoder-transformers
 named ***Tucano***. Our models perform equal or superior to other Portuguese and multilingual language models of similar size in several
 Portuguese benchmarks. The evaluation of our models also reveals that model performance on many currently available benchmarks
 used by the Portuguese NLP community has ***little to no correlation*** with the scaling of token ingestion during
 training, highlighting the limitations of such evaluations when it comes to the assessment of Portuguese generative language models.
 All derivatives of our study are openly released on GitHub and Hugging Face.

Our study brings the following advancements to the Portuguese NLP community:

1. The concatenation of a larger and more **high-quality dataset for Portuguese** language modeling ([**GigaVerbo**](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TucanoBR/GigaVerbo)).
2. The development of **learned filters and datasets** to improve text pre-processing for Portuguese.
3. Pushing self-supervised pretraining beyond the **500 billion tokens** mark for Portuguese monolingual models.
4. The development of new, low-resource, efficient, and effective **open-source language models for Portuguese** ([**Tucano**](https://huggingface.co/collections/TucanoBR/tucano-670565e8c5325fb7f2da4361)).
5. A critical assessment and comparison of currently available **benchmarks for Portuguese language models**.

## An Anthology of Portuguese LLM Development

Our study provides a historical overview of Portuguese LLM development from **2020 to October 2024**, allowing readers to better contextualize our and past works.

![This image illustrates several Portuguese language model releases from 2020 to June 2024.](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/images/timeline.png)

## GigaVerbo

GigaVerbo contains over **145 million documents**, amounting to **780 GB of text**. Much like other text datasets, Gigaverbo was formed by concatenating several portions of openly available datasets for Portuguese and deduplicating their summation.

Our dataset is composed of the following subsets:

| **Subset** | **Nº of Samples** | **%** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **monoHPLT-PT** | 58,244,012 | 40.09% | The clean and deduplicated Portuguese portion of the High-Performance Language Technologies resources dataset. |
| **CrawlPT** | 43,846,974 | 30.17% | A deduplicated Portuguese corpus extracted from various web pages, concatenated from CC-100, Oscar, and BrWaC. |
| **Multilingual-C4** | 16,092,571 | 11.07% | The Brazilian Portuguese cleaned portion of the m-C4 dataset. |
| **Common Crawl** | 12,470,998 | 8.58% | A clean and deduplicated snapshot of the Common Crawl dataset (CC-MAIN-2023-23). |
| **BlogSet-BR** | 4,321,181 | 2.97% | A collection of blog posts written in Brazilian Portuguese. |
| **Instruct-PTBR** | 2,962,856 | 2.04% | A mix of multiple instruction datasets for various tasks, machine-translated from English to Brazilian Portuguese. |
| **Corpus Carolina** | 2,075,395 | 1.43% | An open corpus with varied typology in contemporary Brazilian Portuguese. |
| **UltrachatBR** | 1,255,091 | 0.86% | A Portuguese version (machine-translated) of the Ultrachat dataset. |
| **Wikipedia** | 1,101,475 | 0.76% | Cleaned Portuguese articles built from the Wikipedia dumps. |
| **CulturaX** | 999,994 | 0.69% | The Portuguese portion of CulturaX, a multilingual dataset with 167 languages. |
| **LegalPT** | 925,522 | 0.64% | A concatenation of publicly available legal data in Portuguese, including legislation, jurisprudence, and legal articles. |
| **Gpt4All** | 808,803 | 0.56% | A Portuguese (machine-translated) version of the Gpt4All dataset. |
| **Bactrian-X** | 66,994 | < 0.1% | The Portuguese portion of Bactrian-X, a collection of instruction-response pairs in 52 languages. |
| **XL-Sum** | 64,577 | < 0.1% | A Portuguese (machine-translated) version of XL-Sum, a diverse dataset for abstractive summarization. |
| **Dolly 15K** | 28,401 | < 0.1% | A Portuguese (machine-translated) version of Dolly 15K, an open-source dataset of instruction-following records generated by human annotators. |
| **CosmosQA** | 25,260 | < 0.1% | A Portuguese (machine-translated) version of the CosmosQA dataset for commonsense-based reading comprehension. |
| **ROOTS** | 10,740 | < 0.1% | The Portuguese portion of the ROOTS corpus, a dataset spanning 59 languages. |

GigaVerbo is currently hosted on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TucanoBR/GigaVerbo). More information can be found in its dataset card.

## GigaVerbo Text-Filter

With the help of **GPT-4o**, we scored over **100,000 samples of GigaVerbo in terms of their overall quality**. With these scored samples dataset, we trained classifiers to help us filter GigaVerbo from low-quality samples (our text-quality dataset is also available in [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TucanoBR/GigaVerbo-Text-Filter)).

| **Class** | **Precision** | **Recall** | **F1-score** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **LaBSE + XGBoost** | Low | 0.89 | 0.81 | 0.85 |
| High | 0.92 | 0.96 | 0.94 |
| **BERTimbau** | Low | **0.99** | **0.97** | **0.98** |
| High | **0.99** | **0.99** | **0.99** |

The table above shows the evaluation scores for both our LaBSE + XGBoost and BERTimbau-based classifiers. All these models are available on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR).

Like many other studies, we used a decoder-only Transformer based on the Llama architecture as the basis for our models. For convenience,
 we eventually refer to these models as Tucano *small*, *medium*, *large*, and *XL*,
 which respectively correspond to the **[160m](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-160m)**, **[630m](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-630m)**, **[1b1](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-1b1)**, and **[2b4](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-2b4)** models.

| **\(n_{param}\)** | **\(n_{layers}\)** | **\(d_{model}\)** | **\(d_{mlp}\)** | **\(n_{heads}\)** | **\(n_{KV-heads}\)** | **\(d_{head}\)** | **\(c_{length}\)** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 162,417,408 | 12 | 768 | 3,072 | 12 | 12 | 64 | 2048 |
| 630,253,568 | 14 | 2,048 | 4,096 | 16 | 4 | 128 | 2048 |
| 1,100,048,384 | 22 | 2,048 | 5,632 | 32 | 4 | 64 | 2048 |
| 2,444,618,240 | 24 | 2,560 | 10,240 | 16 | 4 | 160 | 4096 |

Each model has a vocabulary size of 32,000. Tucano-160m, 630m, and 1b1 were trained with a context window of 2048 tokens, while the largest model (2b4) was trained with sequences of length 4096. All models uese the [TeenyTinyLlama](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/TeenyTinyLlama/) tokenizer.

![This image illustrates the training loss and perplexity of Tucano models.](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/images/loss-perplexity.png)

All logs from our training runs recorded the loss, evaluation loss, the current value of the learning rate, and the gradient norm for that specific optimization step. These are all available on [GitHub](https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/Tucano).

## Benchmarks

During training, we saved several checkpoints for each model at intervals of approximately 10.5 billion tokens. For every checkpoint, we employed a comprehensive evaluation harness. This evaluation harness contains several Portuguese native evaluations and English benchmarks machine-translated into Portuguese.

| Benchmark | n-shot | Origin | Type | Metric |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ENEM | 3-shot | Native | Q&A | `acc` |
| BLUEX | 3-shot | Native | Q&A | `acc` |
| OAB Exams | 3-shot | Native | Q&A | `acc` |
| ASSIN2 RTE | 15-shot | Native | Entailment | `f1 macro` |
| ASSIN2 STS | 10-shot | Native | Similarity | `pearson` |
| FAQUAD NLI | 15-shot | Native | Entailment | `f1 macro` |
| HateBR | 25-shot | Native | Classification | `f1 macro` |
| PT Hate Speech | 25-shot | Native | Classification | `f1 macro` |
| TweetSentBR | 25-shot | Native | Classification | `f1 macro` |
| CALAME-PT | 0-shot | Native | Next Word Prediction | `acc` |
| ARC-Challenge | 25-shot | Translated | Q&A | `acc norm` |
| HellaSwag | 10-shot | Translated | Q&A | `acc norm` |
| TruthfulQA | 0-shot | Translated | Q&A | `bleurt` |
| LAMBADA | 0-shot | Translated | Next Word Prediction | `acc` |

To learn how to replicate our usage of this harness, please visit the evaluation section of our [GitHub](https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/Tucano/tree/main/evaluations/README.md) repository.

Our evaluations revealed that for several benchmarks, token ingestions (i.e., *how long a model is pre-trained on new tokens*) seem to **not be correlated to benchmark performance**. Hence, we hypothesize that results showing good performance on such benchmarks (i.e., above what a random guesser would achieve) might indicate not language modeling pretraining but overfitting to the style of evaluation these benchmarks bring.

For example, while certain benchmarks **show no change in performance, regardless of the number of tokens ingested**:

![Evaluation scores as a function of token ingestion for the BLUEX benchmark.](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/images/evals-bluex.png)

Other benchmarks prove to be a **indicator of model improvement in terms of its language modeling capabilities** as pretraining progresses:

![Evaluation scores as a function of token ingestion for the CALAME-PT benchmark.](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/images/evals-calame_pt.png)

## Results

Focusing only on the benchmarks that showed a significant correlation between language modeling pretraining and performance, we see that our largest models **outperformed several multilingual and natively pre-trained LLMs across nearly all benchmarks**, including the recently released Llama-3.2-1b. Our models also outperformed larger multilingual models, such as Bloom-1b7.

| **Average** | **Calame-PT** | **Lambada-PT** | **ARC-PT** | **HellaSwag-PT** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Llama-3.2-3B | 52 | 58.43 | 49.1 | 43.25 | 57.2 |
| **Tucano-2b4** | 43.58 | 59.06 | 37.67 | 30.43 | 47.17 |
| Llama-3.2-1B | 42.95 | 51.83 | 41.02 | 33.5 | 45.44 |
| **Tucano-1b1** | 41.55 | 58.24 | 34.7 | 30.43 | 42.84 |
| Gemma-2b | 40.38 | 51.16 | 39.88 | 37.95 | 32.53 |
| Bloom-1b7 | 40.37 | 55.64 | 31.98 | 30.34 | 43.52 |
| **Tucano-630m** | 39.5 | 56.55 | 33.13 | 28.89 | 39.41 |
| Gemma-2-2b | 39.21 | 56.7 | 47.1 | 24.19 | 28.85 |
| Bloom-1b1 | 38.18 | 52.94 | 30.22 | 29.83 | 39.74 |
| GlórIA-1b3 | 36.05 | 52.79 | 27.71 | 26.67 | 37.04 |
| **Tucano-160m** | 35.14 | 52.31 | 28.16 | 27.01 | 33.07 |
| Xglm-564m | 34.55 | 50.58 | 27.42 | 25.56 | 34.64 |
| Bloom-560m | 34.32 | 49.95 | 25.44 | 24.74 | 37.15 |
| TTL-460m | 33.78 | 49.42 | 23.29 | 29.4 | 33 |
| mGPT-1b3 | 31.81 | 47.14 | 29.92 | 23.81 | 26.37 |
| TTL-160m | 30.78 | 46.72 | 20.98 | 26.15 | 29.29 |
| Lola-v1 | 30.19 | 26.4 | 18.32 | 30.42 | 45.61 |
| GPorTuguese | 28.92 | 40.61 | 22.98 | 22.48 | 29.62 |

Meanwhile, our custom Portuguese evaluation, based on the [AlpacaEval](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/alpaca_eval) methodology, demonstrates that our instruct models, **[Tucano-1b1-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-1b1-Instruct)** and **[Tucano-2b4-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR/Tucano-2b4-Instruct)**,
 produce outputs preferred over much larger models such as **Sabiá-7b** and **Gervásio-7b**.

| **Avg. Length** | **Wins** | **Base Wins** | **Total Matches** | **Length-Controlled Win Rate (%)** | **LC Std. Error** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct | 1609 | 257 | 548 | 805 | 21.06 | 0.075 |
| **Tucano-2b4-Instruct** | 1843 | 151 | 654 | 805 | 13.00 | 0.071 |
| **Tucano-1b1-Instruct** | 1667 | 124 | 681 | 805 | 8.80 | 0.083 |
| Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct | 1429 | 99 | 706 | 805 | 7.15 | 0.057 |
| TeenyTinyLlama-460m-Chat | 1333 | 28 | 777 | 805 | 2.84 | 0.059 |
| Sabiá-7b | 5011 | 1 | 804 | 805 | 0.076 | 0.0043 |
| Gervásio-7b | 5740 | 1 | 804 | 805 | 0.026 | 0.0016 |

All evaluations for all benchmarks that form our custom harness are available on our [GitHub](https://github.com/Nkluge-correa/Tucano/blob/main/evaluations/README.md) repository.

## How To Use

All our models are available on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/TucanoBR), and can easily be used by any application in compliance with the **Apache 2.0 license**.

![Example code to use Tucano models.](https://nkluge-correa.github.io/Tucano/static/images/code-sample.png)

The Tucano series significantly contributes to the Portuguese NLP community in several ways. All **models, along with intermediary checkpoints, datasets, code implementations, and logs, are freely accessible through the repositories associated with this study**, setting the Tucano series apart from several other works.

| **Model** | **Data** | **Code** | **Logs** | **#models** | **#ckpts** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Tucano🟢🟡🔵** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 6 | 111 |
| TeenyTinyLlama | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 3 | 70 |
| GPorTuguese | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 1 | 1 |
| PTT5 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | 6 | 1 |
| RoBERTaLexPT | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | 2 | 3 |
| Albertina | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | 8 | 1 |
| BERTimbau | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | 2 | 1 |
| DeBERTinha | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | 1 | 1 |
| Gervásio | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | 2 | 1 |
| PTT5-v2 | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | 4 | 1 |
| BERTabaporu | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | 2 | 1 |
| Glória | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | 1 | 1 |
| Sabiá | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | 1 | 1 |
| Sabiá-2 | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | 2 | None |
| Sabiá-3 | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | 1 | None |

In terms of open (and reproducible) development, many aspects of past studies are indeed closed. Given the level of computing needed to practice deep learning at such scales, a lack of reusable code and materials can seriously slow down the Portuguese NLP community's progress while hindering its sustainability. With **Tucano** and **GigaVerbo's** development, we hope to make this scenario more sustainable and open.

## Aknowlegments
